symptom: ako/mxcli#2119: `mxcli test --local` while `run --local --watch --test-endpoint` ran: the scratch runtime's after-startup recursed (MicroflowException: java.lang.StackOverflowError), no test ran, and the dev loop's next build failed with CE1613 'MxTest.RegisterEndpoint no longer exists'. After the fix, a following --attach was refused: 'this change needs a runtime restart'.
cause: captureProjectState took the current after-startup microflow, already the dev loop's MxTest.RegisterEndpoint, as the project's own; the test run's endpoint (same name) chained to it, i.e. to itself. With MxTest pre-existing, the endpoint cleanup still dropped RegisterEndpoint, the Java action and its source, then set the setting back to the captured RegisterEndpoint. Separately, a test run that builds rewrites deployment/, which it shares with the dev loop by necessity (mxbuild cannot move it); a hold released over an unchanged model left that deployment as the test run's, and the next attach's build wanted a restart.
file: cmd/mxcli/testrunner/runner.go (projectState.hosted/chain, classifyHostedEndpoint, RestoreAbandonedEndpoint before capture), cmd/mxcli/testrunner/runner_endpoint.go (cleanup leaves a hosted endpoint), cmd/mxcli/docker/watchhold.go (Deployment identity, holdResync), cmd/mxcli/docker/runlocal.go
insight: 'The current after-startup microflow' is not 'the project's after-startup microflow' once anything swaps it; the swapper's restore record is the only place the original lives, so every reader of the setting must consult it. And a cleanup keyed on 'did I create the module' is wrong when someone else owns a document inside it. The follow-on deployment drift was found only by running the next command in the workflow (attach) after the fix, not by the reported reproduction: verify the workflow, not just the repro. Measured: restoring deployment/model/ by copy is not a fix (it trips the stale-model check), so the dev loop resyncs with one build, which after --local was a restart.
